Agent.text:
I've built a new standalone version of the word processor. It never connects to the internet and has no scanning (TWAIN) or sharing features. The build succeeds, Craft Anything's comparison check now passes, and six automatic tests of typing and page layout pass. I also looked at a sample document on screen to confirm the text draws correctly.

**What's in it:**
- The original's menu order (File, Edit, View, Create, Page, Text, Window, Help), with all the internet, scanning and team-sharing commands taken out.
- A single row of new flat, modern icons.
- Documents open in tabs instead of separate windows.
- Real pages with margins, a ruler, headers and footers, and page numbers.
- Text styles, fonts, colours, highlighting, alignment, bullets and numbering.
- Find & Replace with the original's four match options (whole words, starting with, ending with, containing), plus a word count.
- The original's own list of 170 auto-corrections (for example "teh" becomes "the").
- A recovery copy saved every 10 minutes, kept only on this computer.
- Light and dark themes.

As you asked, it always opens at 100% zoom, lets you zoom from 25% to 200%, and starts in 12-point Times New Roman.

**What's different or missing:**
- **Name:** it's called "Scribe Pro". The question about using the "Word Pro" name got no answer, and that name is a trademark.
- **Printing and spell checking aren't included yet.** For now you can save as Rich Text and print from another program.
- **Old files:** it saves its own document files and Rich Text or plain text files, but can't open the old program's own document files. Save those as Rich Text in the old program first.
- **Estimated details:** I couldn't find the original's exact list of font sizes, or how much F4 grows text, so those are my best guesses.

A good next request would be "add printing and a spell checker that works offline".

Agent.text: The check passes. One last sanity look inside the sample PDF to confirm the words are really in it.

I added the common modern features:
- **Spelling:** spell check as you type, using Windows' own offline dictionary, with a right-click menu of suggestions and a Check Spelling window (F7).
- **Formatting and navigation:** a format painter, a line-spacing button and a headings navigation pane.
- **Files and printing:** PDF export, printing (Print makes a PDF and opens it in your PDF viewer, where you print), and opening and saving Word (.docx) files.

As you asked, 17 free fonts now ship with the app (Lora, Merriweather, Roboto, Inter and others, all under a free licence that allows redistribution). The font box is now a wider, searchable list grouped into Serif, Sans Serif, Monospace and Handwriting, with each name shown in its own font. One installed font, Cambria, is hidden because the app can't read the file format Windows stores it in.

The build and all automatic tests pass, and the comparison check passes. I couldn't view a printed PDF as a picture here, so I only confirmed the words land on the right pages inside it.

Agent.text: I'll open the original program again and dig into its code for the values I had to guess (zoom limits, text enlarge step and size list, timed-save interval, undo depth, word counting).
The original program is no longer at C:\lotus\wordpro. Let me see if a copy exists anywhere else or is still loaded.
The original program was removed from the computer, so I'm checking whether its saved Ghidra analysis can still be read.
The saved analysis opens and answers. I'm now searching its text and constants for the guessed settings.
The settings (UndoLevels, AutoSave, Backup, CustomLevel zoom, CycleKeyFontSizes) live in a table of names with values beside them. Dumping that table.
That reader serves a different list. The registry-style settings table starts at 0x8b2988, so I'll find the code that indexes into it.
Several small getter functions index that table. Decompiling them, then finding which are called with the UndoLevels/AutoSave/zoom/font-size numbers.
These getters take (section, setting number, default value). Two calls read UndoLevels (#0x17). Decompiling those and the core reader.
The original's undo setting defaults to **4 levels** (function 0x48e24c reads "UndoLevels" with default 4). Now looking up who reads AutoSave, the zoom CustomLevel and the font-size cycle list.
Most other settings go through table-driven wrappers. Decompiling those.
A lookup (0x448848) maps each setting to its section, name and default (0x4492b8). Decompiling those to reach the defaults table.
The zoom menu code only lists command numbers. The custom-zoom range should show up where the "number between %s and %s" message (#15517) is raised, so I'm searching for that.
This is a general range-checker; its limits come from whoever creates it. Tracing its creators.
Zoom limits are already settled by your answer (25–200%), so I'll stop chasing them. Next: what F4 "Enlarge Text" really does.
No built-in table of font sizes exists in the program, so that list stays an estimate. A couple more lookups: word counting and SmartCorrect.
